layoutProps.alt: Coffee beans tumbling behind the round window of a roasting drum, glowing brown.
layoutProps.lead: A roast takes about twelve minutes and decides much of a coffee's taste. Follow one batch through our roaster.

props.figureAlt: A drum roaster in section: a hopper on top, a drum of beans over a row of flames, a chimney and a chaff collector, and a round cooling tray beside it.

items.title: Load the hopper
items.markdown: The roaster weighs a batch of green beans and pours it into the hopper. When the drum is hot enough, a gate drops the beans in: that is the charge.

items.title: Turn in the drum
items.markdown: The drum turns so that every bean moves through the hot air and touches the hot metal evenly. A probe among the beans gives their temperature.

items.title: Steer the heat
items.markdown: Gas burners under the drum heat it. The roaster turns the flame up or down, minute by minute, to follow the profile written for this coffee.

items.title: Cool them fast
items.markdown: At the end the beans fall into the cooling tray, where arms stir them and a fan pulls cold air through. Within minutes they stop roasting.

props.figureAlt: A graph of the beans' temperature, upwards, over twelve minutes of roasting, across.

items.title: Drying
items.alt: The curve dips after the charge, then climbs through a band shaded yellow: the drying.
items.markdown: Cold beans cool the drum at first: their temperature dips, then climbs. For four or five minutes they lose water and turn from green to pale yellow, smelling of hay.

items.title: Browning
items.alt: The curve climbs more slowly through a band shaded light brown: the browning.
items.markdown: From about 150 °C, sugars and proteins react and the beans turn brown, smelling of toast and caramel. The roaster eases the heat and the curve climbs more slowly.

items.title: First crack
items.alt: A burst marks the curve near the top: the first crack.
items.markdown: At around 200 °C, steam inside the beans breaks them open with a crack like popcorn. From here on, every few seconds change the flavour.

items.title: Development, then drop
items.alt: The curve ends in a last band, the development, and an arrow down: the drop.
items.markdown: The time after first crack is the development: a minute or two for a light roast, longer for a dark one. Then the beans drop into the cooling tray.

props.caption: The same beans before and after: roasted, they are larger, lighter in the hand and brown.

props.stem: Complete what happens in the roaster.
props.markdown: While drying, the beans lose [[water]]. Then sugars and proteins react and the beans turn [[brown]]. At first crack, [[steam]] breaks them open, and the time after it is the [[development]].

feedback.correct: Yes: water out, browning, then steam cracks the beans, and the development after it sets the roast level.
feedback.incorrect: Follow the curve again: what leaves the beans first, what colour comes with the browning, and what is trapped inside them until it cracks them open?

props.alt: Freshly roasted dark beans, edge to edge.
props.title: Let them rest
props.markdown: Fresh beans give off carbon dioxide for days, and the gas pushes the water away from the grounds. We rest ours a few days before we brew them.
